title: Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (G.17, September 2026 data) — 9:15 a.m. ET, the quiet end of the set: the month-3 print, on an opex Friday, with no nowcast vintage
source: FED: two independent federalreserve.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 — the Board's G.17 announcements feed (feeds/g17.html, HTTP 200, 614,006 bytes) states verbatim "In 2026, the G.17 release on Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization will be published at 9:15 a.m. on January 16, February 18, March 16, April 16, May 15, June 15, July 17, August 18, September 18, October 16, November 17, and December 16", and the Board's own release-date table (releases/g17/release_dates.htm — note the underscore; the g17_release_dates.htm path sibling lanes tried still 404s) carries the row "October 2026 | 16-October-2026" in a table whose footer reads "Last Update: August 18, 2026" and whose 2025 rows still read "October 2025 NA" / "November 2025 NA" from the funding lapse, i.e. it is maintained rather than stale. The same date is restated a third time inside the current release itself (releases/g17/current/default.htm, HTTP 200, 115,934 bytes). PROMOTED from the estimate filed by the nahb-hmi-2026-10-19 sweep, which said in its own notes that it could not self-confirm an in-sweep discovery and that the precedent for promotion was available in one step to whichever lane researched this id — this is that session, reading the Federal Reserve primaries directly. The Board's verb is "will be published", not the "anticipated" that keeps the Census siblings at estimate. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research, after reading the single proposal that existed for this id (proposals/industrial-production-2026-10-16.from-nahb-hmi-2026-10-19.json, now shadowed and inert). Every claim in that proposal was re-derived rather than carried. The reference month is SEPTEMBER 2026 — month 3 of the Q3-2026 quarter GDPNow is still nowcasting on this date (it rolls to Q4 on 2026-10-29) — and that is structural, not an accident of this year: 14 of the 15 October editions in the Board's 189-date archive carry September data, and the 15th (2021-10-18, feed-titled "August 2021") is a mis-titled announcement, since 2021-09-15 already carried August and 2021-11-16 resumed at October. This print therefore COMPLETES THE POSITION SET the calendar tracks for one series: month 1 (industrial-production-2026-11-17), month 2 (industrial-production-2026-12-16), month 3 (this one) — and month 3 is measurably the quietest of the three. Re-derived this session from the Board's 189-date archive joined to ContribArchives (1,871 vintages, 1,822 same-quarter deltas, 143 G.17 vintages, matching both siblings): month-3 vintages move the GDP nowcast a median 0.0975pp (n=48) against 0.0862pp for the 1,679 non-G.17 vintages — permutation p=0.6456, i.e. INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM AN ORDINARY DAY — while month 1 reads 0.3524pp (p<0.0001 against month 3) and month 2 0.2026pp (p=0.0147). The report's own Equipment channel moves 0.0071pp (p=0.2205) and never once reached 0.10pp in any of the 48. The Atlanta Fed agrees from the publisher's side and more strongly than for either sibling: its PostedUpdates sheet schedules NO GDPNow vintage on 2026-10-16 at all — it schedules 2026-10-15 (retail sales + PPI) and 2026-10-20 (housing starts) and skips this date, so September IP is absorbed four days later rather than on its own morning. On the tape (SPY 2014-05-01 -> 2026-09-04, non-G.17 baseline n=2,961) the all-G.17 overnight-gap elevation (0.3624% vs 0.2822%, p=0.0075) is again entirely the 08:30 retail co-release: with-retail 0.4285% (p=0.0038, n=59), without 0.3109% (p=0.4731, n=83). This date's one distinguishing feature is that it is OCTOBER OPEX, and that survives its own control in the same shape — a G.17 on an opex Friday reads 0.4598% against 0.2983% for an opex Friday without one (p=0.0245, n=33), but split by co-release it is with-retail 0.5173% (p=0.0707, n=10) and without-retail 0.3368% (p=0.6692, n=22). Retail sales print 2026-10-15, the day BEFORE this one, so this print sits in the null cell: month-3, no retail, n=30, gap 0.3196% (p=0.5423), range 0.6602% (p=0.0775, narrower than baseline). Impact LOW and symbols empty on those measured grounds, not by default; no macro-keyed house playbook exists (grep of trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md re-run 2026-09-06, 0 hits) and no instrument attaches. Funding is not a live variable here the way it is for the December twin: PL 119-103 funds through 2026-12-11, well after this print. The live variable is the ANNUAL REVISION the Board announced 2026-05-15 for "the autumn of 2026" (base year to 2022, 2023 Census manufacturing benchmark, capacity through Q4-2025) with no date as of 2026-09-06 — but this session bounds it where the siblings could not: all 12 revisions on record are month-end releases (11 at day-of-month >= 21, the twelfth 2016-04-01, the day after March 31), none mid-month, and the minimum dated-notice lead is 11 days, so a revision preempting a 16th-of-the-month print would need its notice by 2026-10-05. Deliberately NOT proposed: the 2027 editions the Board has already scheduled (real and dated, but standalone with no known vintage — the same grounds on which the November and December lanes declined 09-18 and 10-16 respectively, and 09-18 already exists as another lane's proposal), and the annual revision itself, which still has no date. Date confirmed; nothing here licenses an entry.
